hub.title: Everything a Coworker needs to do the job.
hub.lede: Memory, skills, apps and a computer of its own. Here is what each Coworker comes with, and how you stay in control of it.
hub.metaTitle: Features: Everything an AI Coworker Comes With
hub.metaDescription: Memory, skills, apps and a computer of its own: every feature a Rerun Coworker comes with, from the Chief of Staff to security, and how you keep control.

all.title: Every feature
all.lead: {count, plural, one {# feature} other {# features}}, in four groups: who your Coworkers are, how they work, where you follow them, and how you keep control.

included.title: Included in Pro

lines.3: A private machine in the cloud
lines.6: Your own AI at no extra cost

included.extras: LinkedIn Pro and WhatsApp Pro are paid apps, and more credits come in packs of {packCredits} for {packPrice}.

1.question: Are all these features in one plan?
1.answer: Yes. Pro has every feature on this page, with unlimited Coworkers and seats and {monthlyCredits} Rerun credits a month. Only LinkedIn Pro, WhatsApp Pro, extra credits and templates with a price of their own are billed apart.

2.question: Can I try them before I pay?
2.answer: Yes. The {trialDays}-day trial opens every feature, with {trialAgents} Coworkers running at once and no limit on seats.

3.question: Do I need to set each feature up?
3.answer: No. The Chief of Staff builds your Coworkers with their apps, skills and routines from what you tell it. You connect your accounts when a Coworker asks for them.

4.question: Can I run Rerun on my own servers?
4.answer: Yes. Rerun is open source under AGPL-3.0 and runs on your own server with Docker. A self-hosted install has the Coworkers, memory, skills, routines and apps, but not what only a hosted service offers: the included credits, LinkedIn Pro, WhatsApp Pro and paid data.

templates.lead: Ready-made Coworkers from the library, installed in a minute.

coworkers.title: Hire an AI Coworker, not a workflow.
coworkers.lede: Give it a job in one sentence. It gets its own memory, skills, apps and computer, runs on its own schedule and tells you what it did.
coworkers.metaTitle: AI Coworkers: AI Agents That Hold a Job
coworkers.metaDescription: A Rerun Coworker is an AI agent hired for one job, with its own memory, skills, apps and cloud computer. It runs on a schedule and reports back every time.
coworkers.caption: A Coworker at work on its own screen, then saying what it just did.

1.title: Describe the job
1.body: Tell your Chief of Staff what you need in one sentence, or install a ready-made Coworker from the template library.

2.title: It sets itself up
2.body: It writes its soul, its skills and its schedule, then shows a card for each app it needs you to sign in to.

3.title: It works and reports back
3.body: Each run leaves a thread with what it did. It stops to ask when it needs you, and remembers each correction.

memory.title: Its own memory
memory.line: It writes down durable facts and recalls them later. Correct it once and it remembers the correction.

skills.title: Its own skills
skills.line: Written procedures it opens only when a task matches, so its prompt stays short as it learns more.

computer.title: Its own computer
computer.line: A screen in the cloud with a browser, files and a terminal. Watch it live, or take control.

routines.title: Its own routines
routines.line: A schedule in plain words, like every weekday at 8am, or a webhook another service calls.

1.question: What is an AI Coworker?
1.answer: An agent you hire for one job instead of a workflow you draw. It has a name, a soul that says what it owns, its own memory, skills, files and database, the apps it needs and its routines. It does that job run after run and records every step.

2.question: Do I need to write prompts or code?
2.answer: No. Describe the job in plain words and the Coworker writes its own soul, skills and schedule. Everything it set up stays readable and editable on its card: Settings, Skills, Routines and Apps.

3.question: How many Coworkers can I have?
3.answer: As many as you need: Pro has no limit. The {trialDays}-day trial runs {trialAgents} at once, and the others are built and wait, switched off, until Pro starts.

4.question: Can I change a Coworker once it is set up?
4.answer: Yes. Edit its soul in Settings, switch off a capability it has no business using, change its model per conversation, or ask it to rewrite its own instructions. Changes apply on its next run.

5.question: Can I copy a Coworker that works well?
5.answer: Yes. Duplicate copies it into the same workspace with its skills, memories, files, apps and routines. Share creates a link for someone outside the workspace: keys, connected accounts and chat history never travel with it.

chief-of-staff.title: A Chief of Staff that runs your AI team.
chief-of-staff.lede: Say what you need and it briefs the right Coworker, or builds one. It checks in on its own, answers your inbox once you say how, and takes the name you give it.

chief-of-staff.metaDescription: The Rerun Chief of Staff builds your team of AI Coworkers, briefs the right one, checks in daily, answers their questions in your name, by text or voice.

1.title: Tell it about your business
1.body: During onboarding it reads your website, fills the Brain and proposes a starter team for your kind of business.

2.title: Ask in plain words
2.body: Click its orb, press ⌘K or hold Space. It builds a Coworker, sends a task to the right one and follows the run.

3.title: Let it check in
3.body: It looks at your workspace on its own. When something deserves your time, it opens a thread with one next step.

voice.title: Hold Space and talk

inbox.title: It answers your inbox
inbox.line: Tell it what to say and it answers your Coworkers’ questions, approvals and skill proposals in your name.

check-ins.title: Daily check-ins
check-ins.line: It reads the runs, the Brain and the shared data, changes nothing, and writes only when something is worth it.

chief-of-staff.templatesTitle: Give it a team to run.

1.question: What is the Chief of Staff?
1.answer: The assistant every workspace comes with. It knows every Coworker, what each one does and what it is working on. It builds new ones, briefs them, explains a failed run, keeps the Brain with you and answers questions about Rerun from the docs.

2.question: Is it the same as the Coworker manager?
2.answer: Yes. The Coworker manager is now called the Chief of Staff, and it does more: it builds your first team, checks in on its own and answers your inbox. Same page, same place in a corner of the board.

3.question: Can I give it a name?
3.answer: Yes. It offers to take one early in a conversation, and an admin can change it on its card. The name belongs to the workspace: every member sees it in the list, the chat and the shortcuts. Empty the field to go back to Chief of Staff.

4.question: What happens during a check-in?
4.answer: Once a day, during your working hours, it reads your Coworkers, their runs, the Brain and the shared data. It changes nothing. If something needs you, it opens a thread with what it saw and one suggested step, and sends it to your phone.

5.question: Will it approve things without me?
5.answer: Only what you told it to answer. It asks for your yes in its chat before approving a spend, and it never types a key, signs in to an app or takes over a browser in your name: those stay with you.

1.question: How does one Coworker hand work to another?
1.answer: It messages the other by its @handle, the way you would, and passes on what it found. The other works in a thread of its own and answers back. A Coworker woken by the end of a job picks up from there.

2.question: Do I have to wire the chain myself?
2.answer: No. Write in each soul what it owns and who comes next, or ask the Chief of Staff to set the team up. It knows who handles what and briefs the right one.

3.question: Where do they keep what they share?
3.answer: In the shared database and the shared folder, both under Brain, common to every Coworker of the workspace. Each one also keeps a private database and folder that no other Coworker can read.

4.question: Can one Coworker split a big task?
4.answer: Yes. With Delegate on, it hands self-contained subtasks to throwaway sub-coworkers that work in its own folder, on its own files, and it gathers what they bring back.

5.question: Is this a multi-agent workflow builder?
5.answer: It solves the same problem without a canvas. There are no nodes to maintain: you hire Coworkers for jobs, and the work moves between them the way it moves in a team.

second-brain.title: A second brain for your business.
second-brain.lede: What you sell, to whom, at what price and in what voice, written once in pages every Coworker reads before it works. Filled from your website, kept current with you.

2.title: Import what you have
2.body: Drop files, a .zip or a whole folder. A .zip is unpacked with its folders, filed under the Box and tags you pick.

second-brain.abilitiesTitle: Written once, read by every Coworker.

pages.title: Pages you edit in place

1.question: What goes into the Brain?
1.answer: What you would tell a new hire: what you sell and at what price, who buys it, your team, your voice, your tools and your priorities, plus pages for customers, competitors, products and decisions. It also holds the shared folder and the shared database.

2.question: Can I import the documents I already have?
2.answer: Yes. Drop files, a .zip archive or a folder in the Files section or in a Box. A .zip is unpacked into a folder named after it, its own folders kept. You see the list, and can remove a file, before you click Import.

3.question: Can a Coworker change a page on its own?
3.answer: No. A fact it finds itself becomes a proposal you Accept or Dismiss, and a dismissed change is never proposed again. A fact you tell it in the chat is written at once, with Undo.

4.question: What if a page gets overwritten?
4.answer: Every change is kept. Open Version history from the More menu of the page, pick a version and click Restore this version. The current version stays in the history.

5.question: How is the Brain different from a Coworker’s memory?
5.answer: The Brain is what the whole workspace knows about the company. A Coworker’s memory holds facts about its own work, and fades when nothing uses it. What a person wrote or confirmed in the Brain wins over memory.

1.question: What is computer use?
1.answer: A Coworker sees and drives its own screen: it clicks, types and scrolls in its browser, its files and its terminal. It is how it uses a portal with no API, filling forms and reading results the way a person does.

2.question: Can I watch what it is doing?
2.answer: Yes. The thumbnail on its card shows the screen live while it works. Click it to open the desktop in a window, or Take control to drive it yourself, then let it carry on.

3.question: How does it sign in to my accounts?
3.answer: It asks you for a turn on the screen: Open browser opens its browser for you, you sign in or solve the captcha, then click Done. What you signed in to stays in that Coworker’s browser.

4.question: Does the AI see the passwords it types?
4.answer: No. A secret is stored on your workspace’s machine under a variable name. The Coworker types it into a page by that name, and the value never enters the conversation or reaches the model.

5.question: Do my Coworkers share one computer?
5.answer: They share the workspace’s machine, and each one gets its own screen, its own browser with its own sign-ins, its own folder and its own database.

files.title: Your files stay put

pause.title: Pause in one click

1.question: Why link my own computer?
1.answer: For the work that belongs on your machine: video editing, your GPU, local models, files too big to move. The Coworker stays in the cloud, and your computer only runs what it is asked, while the desktop app is running.

2.question: What can a Coworker run without asking?
2.answer: In the default mode, only the programs you clicked Always allow for. Every new program asks, so does a path outside your working folder, and the places where secrets live always ask, even in Full access.

3.question: Which computers can I link?
3.answer: Any computer that runs the desktop app: a Mac on macOS 13 or later, a PC on Windows 10 or later (in beta), or a Linux x64 machine.

4.question: What happens when my laptop goes to sleep?
4.answer: A running job keeps the computer awake, but a closed lid still puts it to sleep: the job goes on when it wakes. Closing the app’s window keeps jobs running; quitting the app stops them, after asking you.

5.question: Can my teammates use my computer?
5.answer: Everyone in the workspace can use a linked computer through their Coworkers, and each new program still asks for a yes. An admin, or the person who linked it, changes its settings or removes it, which stops everything at once.

1.question: Which tools are in the {connectors}+?
1.answer: The library holds the apps a business runs on: Gmail and Outlook, the calendars, Slack, CRMs like HubSpot, Stripe, Shopify, Notion, the drives and the ad platforms. Hosted MCP servers reach the rest.

2.question: What if my tool is not in the library?
2.answer: Register its MCP server yourself from the MCP tab, or click Request an app under the library. If it has no API at all, the Coworker opens it on its own screen and clicks through it.

3.question: Do connected apps cost extra?
3.answer: No. Every app of the library is in the plan, and so is any MCP server or API you wire yourself. Only LinkedIn Pro and WhatsApp Pro are sold apart, per connected account.

4.question: How much do LinkedIn Pro and WhatsApp Pro cost?
4.answer: Each connected account takes one slot: {linkedinPrice} a month for LinkedIn Pro, {whatsappPrice} a month for WhatsApp Pro, on the same invoice as your plan, whatever the number of Coworkers that use it. During the trial, one slot per app costs nothing until Pro starts.

5.question: Is my LinkedIn account at risk?
5.answer: Each account has a recommended daily pace of invitations and profile views. Past it, the Coworker still does what you ask and warns you once. If LinkedIn itself asks the account to slow down, Coworkers stop using it for a day.

6.question: Can a Coworker call an API that has no app?
6.answer: Yes. It asks for the key through a masked form, then calls the API from its machine, naming the key as $'{VARIABLE_NAME}'. The value resolves at run time and never reaches the model.

7.question: Does every Coworker get every app?
7.answer: Only the ones you pick. An app lives in the Vault: switch it on for the Coworkers that need it, or for Every coworker. An app installed from one Coworker is switched on for that Coworker only.

1.question: How is paid data billed?
1.answer: Each call is paid from your Rerun credits. Pro includes {monthlyCredits} credits every month, and a pack of {packCredits} credits costs {packPrice}, never expires and is drawn on once the month’s credits are spent.

2.question: Will a Coworker spend credits without asking?
2.answer: Not by default. It shows the estimated cost and waits for your yes. Always allow, or Spend without asking in its Capabilities, lets scheduled runs buy data while you are away. Turn it back off at any time.

3.question: Can I use my own Apollo, Clay or Prospeo account?
3.answer: Yes. Apollo, Prospeo and Clay are apps of the library: connect your account once and the Coworker works through it, on your plan with that provider, without spending Rerun credits.

4.question: Does reading LinkedIn profiles cost credits?
4.answer: Not with LinkedIn Pro: the Coworker reads LinkedIn with your account first, at no credit. It buys LinkedIn data only for what your account cannot read, or once the account is past its daily pace, and tells you why.

5.question: Is paid data on a self-hosted install?
5.answer: No. A self-hosted Rerun sells no data. Add providers like Apollo or Semrush there as apps or MCP servers, with your own API keys.

1.question: Which systems does the desktop app run on?
1.answer: macOS 13 or later on Apple Silicon or Intel, Windows 10 or later on x64 or Arm (in beta), and Linux x64 as an AppImage, a .deb or a .rpm. It updates itself.

2.question: What does Quick ask do?
2.answer: It opens a field for your Chief of Staff over whatever app you are in. Type and press Enter, or hold Space to talk, and the app opens on the answer.

3.question: Can I change the Quick ask shortcut?
3.answer: Yes. In your account, under Desktop app, click the Quick ask shortcut and press the keys you want. It needs ⌘, ⌥ or ⌃ (Ctrl or Alt on Windows and Linux). Press ⌫ instead to turn Quick ask off.

4.question: Is it different from the web app?
4.answer: It is the same app, updated at the same time, plus what a browser tab cannot do: Quick ask, the Coworker dock, system notifications, several windows, and linking this computer to your workspace.

5.question: Does it work with a self-hosted Rerun?
5.answer: Yes. Click Change Server… in the Rerun menu on a Mac, or the File menu on Windows and Linux, and enter your server’s address. Use Rerun Cloud brings you back.

1.body: Continue with Apple, Google, your phone or your email. Your workspace, Coworkers and conversations are already there.

2.title: Turn on notifications

mobile-app.templatesTitle: Coworkers you check on from your phone.

1.question: Is there an Android app?
1.answer: Yes. Rerun is on the App Store for iPhone and iPad, and on Google Play for Android. Both open the same workspace as the web app, and a message sent from one shows up on the other.

2.question: Can I approve something without opening the app?
2.answer: On an iPhone, yes: touch and hold the notification, tap Approve, Deny, Answer or Reply, and Face ID confirms. On Android the buttons unlock the phone and open Rerun. An app to connect or a key always opens the app.

3.question: What does the widget show?
3.answer: On the home screen, whoever needs you (small) or your crew at work (medium). On the lock screen, a line above the clock, three lines under it, or the face of whoever waits. A tap opens the conversation.

4.question: What can I not do on my phone?
4.answer: Settings that need a bigger screen, such as billing, stay in the web app. The rest is there: conversations, approvals, files, apps, routines, the model picker and your notification settings.

5.question: Can I start the trial from my phone?
5.answer: Yes. A trial started from the mobile app needs no card: it runs for {trialDays} days and stops at its end unless you add one.

runs-24-7.metaTitle: AI Agents That Run 24/7 on Servers in Europe
runs-24-7.metaDescription: Each Rerun workspace runs on its own private machine in Europe. Coworkers start on schedules, webhooks and LinkedIn or WhatsApp replies, laptop shut.
runs-24-7.caption: The same workspace at 7am and at 3am: the run happens either way.

1.title: Describe the schedule
1.body: In its Routines, click New and type every weekday at 8am or tomorrow at 3pm. It becomes a schedule in your timezone.

2.title: Or give it a webhook
2.body: Create a trigger, copy its Webhook URL and paste it in Stripe or any service. Each call starts a run with the payload.

3.title: Read the run in the morning
3.body: Each automated run opens its own thread. If it needs you at 3am, it pauses and waits for your answer.

runs-24-7.templatesTitle: Coworkers that work while you sleep.

1.question: Does my computer need to stay on?
1.answer: No. Your Coworkers run on your workspace’s machine in the cloud, not on your laptop. Close it, fly somewhere, and the Monday morning run still happens.

2.question: Where are the servers?
2.answer: In Europe. Each workspace has a private machine there, isolated from every other account, and that is where your Coworkers work and keep what they need between runs.

3.question: Does a scheduled run remember the last one?
3.answer: Each run opens a fresh thread. What carries over is the Coworker’s memory and its database, so a task that must know where it left off writes it down there.

4.question: Can I test a routine before it goes live?
4.answer: Yes. Test Run fires the task right away, even while it is switched off, and leaves its schedule alone.

5.question: What if a webhook URL leaks?
5.answer: The URL is the credential, so click Rotate the secret: the old URL stops working at once, and you paste the new one wherever the trigger is called from.

human-in-the-loop.title: Autonomous, until it needs a yes.
human-in-the-loop.lede: Your Coworker works alone and stops before anything consequential: a send, a spend, a command. It asks in one card, waits, and anyone on the team can answer.
human-in-the-loop.metaTitle: Human in the Loop: Your AI Agent Asks First

human-in-the-loop.caption: Approval required: three reminders to send, Approve or Not now on each one.

1.title: It stops and asks
1.body: Before a consequential step, it shows a card: a question, an approval, a spend or a sign-in. The thread reads Needs you.

2.title: You answer from anywhere
2.body: From the chat, the inbox, the desktop dock or a push on your phone. Anyone who can use its Box can answer.

3.title: It picks up where it stopped
3.body: Approve and the run carries on from your answer. Explain declines with a reason the Coworker reads.

1.question: What does a Coworker stop for?
1.answer: Spending credits waits for an approval unless you allow it. For the rest, its soul says what counts as consequential, like sending to a customer, deleting records or publishing, so you decide how much rope it has.

2.question: Who can answer a request?
2.answer: Anyone who can use the Coworker’s Box. Seats cost nothing, so the person who should decide can be the one who decides.

3.question: What happens if nobody answers?
3.answer: The run waits, and the thread keeps its Needs you badge. A run started at 3am pauses the same way and resumes from your answer whenever you give it. Nothing is skipped because nobody was watching.

4.question: Can the Chief of Staff answer for me?
4.answer: Yes, once you tell it what to say. It answers questions, approvals and skill proposals in your name, the way the inbox does, and asks you first before approving a spend.

5.question: Can I turn a kind of pause off?
5.answer: Yes. Each pause comes from a capability, like Ask you questions or Request approval. Switch it off in the Coworker’s Capabilities and it can no longer pause that way.

1.question: Can I use my Claude or ChatGPT subscription?
1.answer: Yes. Under AI providers, click Add subscription and sign in to Claude Pro or Max, or ChatGPT Plus or Pro. Coworkers on it spend no Rerun credits. Connecting one needs an active plan or a running trial.

2.question: Can I run an open-source or self-hosted model?
2.answer: Yes, through a Custom endpoint: any server that speaks the OpenAI chat format, at an address your workspace’s machine can reach. OpenRouter also carries open models on your own key.

3.question: What happens when my plan hits its limit?
3.answer: The Coworker carries on with the first backup in your list, in the same conversation, and a line says which model took over. Once the plan resets, it goes back. Rerun credit as last resort stays off unless you turn it on.

4.question: What is reasoning effort?
4.answer: How long a model thinks before it answers: Default, Low, Medium or High, from the settings icon on its row in the picker. It is there for Claude, OpenAI and Google models; the Rerun model runs at the level its provider picks.

5.question: What do Rerun credits pay for?
5.answer: The Rerun model and paid data. Pro includes {monthlyCredits} credits every month. A Coworker on your own key or subscription costs nothing on the Rerun side.

security.title: Your data, backed up and kept apart.

1.title: A machine of your own
1.body: Your workspace runs on a private machine in Europe, isolated from every other account. Nothing crosses workspaces.

2.title: Keys in masked forms
2.body: When a Coworker needs a key, it opens a masked form. The value goes to the machine and never enters the chat.

3.title: Backed up every night
3.body: Each night the machine of a paid workspace is backed up, encrypted and stored away from it. We restore on request.

backups.title: Nightly encrypted backups
backups.line: Coworkers, memories, skills, files, databases and the Vault, taken during the night of your time zone.

secrets.title: Secrets the model never sees
secrets.line: The Coworker gets a variable name and uses $'{NAME}': the value resolves on the machine at run time.

spending.line: One switch in Billing stops all spending of Rerun credits. Coworkers on your own AI keep working.

open-source.title: Open source, AGPL-3.0
open-source.line: Read the code Rerun Cloud runs, or host it yourself on your own server with Docker.

1.question: Where is my data stored?
1.answer: On your workspace’s private machine, in Europe, isolated from every other account. Credentials stay on that machine: Rerun’s database keeps only the name of each variable, never the value.

2.question: How are backups handled?
2.answer: Each night of your time zone, Rerun backs up the machine of every paid workspace, encrypted and stored away from it. A Coworker in the middle of a run is never cut off. If something goes wrong, write to help@rerun.build and we restore it.

3.question: Is a key I give a Coworker sent to the model?
3.answer: No. It goes through a masked form straight to the machine, and the Coworker only learns which variable was filled. Never paste a secret in the chat itself: the conversation is stored and sent to the model.

4.question: Can a Coworker spend money on its own?
4.answer: Paid data waits for your yes on an estimated cost, unless you allow a Coworker to spend without asking. The Allow spending switch in Billing stops every credit spend at once, for the Rerun model and for paid data.

5.question: Can I read the code or host it myself?
5.answer: Yes. Rerun is open source under AGPL-3.0: the same product Rerun Cloud runs, for you to host on your own server, with no plan, no credit and no limit on Coworkers or seats.

workspaces.templatesTitle: Coworkers the whole team leans on.

1.question: How much does an extra seat cost?
1.answer: Nothing. Neither Pro nor the trial limits seats, so invite the whole team, including the people who only answer a question once a week.

2.question: When should I use several workspaces?
2.answer: When the businesses share nothing: an agency with one per client, a founder with a company and a side project. For one business with several teams, use Boxes inside one workspace instead.

3.question: Does each workspace need its own plan?
3.answer: Yes. A workspace is one plan, one machine and one set of members, which is what keeps it apart from the others. Switch between them from the pill in the top left corner.

4.question: Can I keep a Box private?
4.answer: Yes. Right-click it, pick Manage access, then Only selected people. Can use chats with its Coworkers and sees their work; Can manage also edits, moves and deletes them. Admins always reach every Box.

5.question: Can a colleague talk to a Coworker I hired?
5.answer: Yes, if they can use its Box. A Coworker belongs to the workspace, not to the person who created it: anyone with access can give it work, read what it did and answer its questions.
